previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: A 68-year-old male with a history of stroke, tracheostomy, G-tube, atrial fibrillation on anticoagulation, diabetes, and recurrent infections was admitted for septic shock due to a Proteus mirabilis urinary tract infection. He presented with hypotension, leukocytosis, and acute kidney injury following a blocked Foley catheter. He was treated in the ICU with IV fluids, dopamine, and broad-spectrum antibiotics, then transitioned to ceftriaxone once culture results were available. His renal function and blood pressure normalized, and he was weaned off vasopressors. Pain and neuropsychiatric medications were held initially due to drug interactions but were safely restarted. He improved clinically, completed a course of IV antibiotics, and was discharged to extended care with plans to finish treatment and monitor INR.

INDICATION:  ___ man with CVA with occluded GJ tube, for unclogging
replacement of GJ tube.

OPERATORS:  Dr. ___ (fellow) and Dr. ___ (attending
radiologist).  Dr. ___ was present and supervising throughout the
procedure.

PROCEDURE AND FINDINGS:  Initial scout imaging demonstrated GJ tube in a
satisfactory position.  Small amount of saline was then injected through the
tube, and after small initial resistance free flow of fluid was noted.  Small
amount of contrast was then injected which demonstrated expected opacification
of a jejunal loop.  The tube was flushed with saline and secured with
StatLock.  Sterile dressings were applied.

Patient tolerated the procedure well.  No immediate post-procedure
complications were noted.

IMPRESSION:  Successful unclogging of the GJ tube and fluoroscopic contrast
study.  The tube is ready to use.
